name: The Sun
description: Our own star — the only one we can study up close, and the baseline every other star on this page is measured against.

name: Proxima Centauri
description: The closest known star to the Sun, a faint red dwarf too dim to see without a telescope despite its proximity. It hosts at least one known exoplanet, Proxima b.

name: Sirius
description: The brightest star in Earth's night sky, a hot white star with a faint white dwarf companion, Sirius B.

name: Betelgeuse
description: A massive, aging red supergiant marking Orion's shoulder. It is expected to end its life in a supernova — though the exact timing is unpredictable and could be anywhere from now to well over 100,000 years from now.

name: Rigel
description: A brilliant blue supergiant marking Orion's foot, tens of thousands of times more luminous than the Sun.

name: Polaris
description: The current North Star, nearly aligned with Earth's rotational axis — a coincidence of timing, since axial precession means the pole slowly points toward different stars over roughly 26,000 years.

name: Vega
description: One of the brightest and most-studied stars in the sky, and a former (and future) pole star due to Earth's axial precession.
